name: GO Classes CS 2025 | ALL INDIA MOCK TEST 3

question.text:
Zebadiah has 3 red shirts, 3 blue shirts, and 3 green shirts in a drawer. Without looking, he randomly pulls shirts from his drawer one at a time. He would like a set of shirts that includes either 3 of the same colour or 3 of different colours. What is the minimum number of shirts that Zebadiah has to pull out to guarantee that he has such a set?

  1. 4
  2. 3
  3. 6
  4. 5

Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence:

It was her view that the country’s problem had been _________ by foreign technocrats, so that to invite them to come back would be counter-productive.

  1. identified
  2. ascertained
  3. exacerbated 
  4. analysed

A piece of paper is folded in half, creating two layers of paper. The paper is then folded in half again. This is continued until the paper has been folded in half a total of five times. The total number of layers of paper in the folded sheet is

  1. 16
  2. 32
  3. 25
  4. 8

Nine students are sitting side by side in one row in the library while their teacher conducts an online lesson from her home. The teacher sees the class from her laptop screen as shown.


Each student is using a different computer, but the teacher's screen shows who each student is sitting next to.
Which student is sitting in the middle (5th position) of the row in the library?

  1. Raul
  2. Lee
  3. Busara
  4. Hannah

The figure below shows the graph of the function $\mathrm{f}$ defined by $f(x)=|2 x|+4,$ for all numbers $x$.

$

($Note $: |2 x|$ is the absolute value of $2 x )$

For which of the following functions $g$ defined for all numbers $x$ does the graph of $g$ intersect the graph of $f?$

  1. $g(x)=x-2$
  2. $g(x)=x+3$
  3. $g(x)=2 x+3$
  4. $g(x)=3 x-2$

Tallulah is playing a game in which she rolls a single standard die once. If the number rolled is $1,2,3$, or 4 , then she wins. If the number rolled is 5 or 6 , then she loses. What is the probability that she loses?

  1. $\frac{1}{3}$
  2. $\frac{5}{6}$
  3. $\frac{1}{2}$
  4. $\frac{1}{6}$

In the $3 \times 3$ table shown, the numbers 1, 2 and 3 are placed so that each number occurs only once in each row and only once in each column.

$$
\begin{array}{|l|l|l|}
\hline & & 1 \\
\hline 3 & X & \\
\hline & & Y \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$


The value of $X+Y$ is

  1. 2
  2. 5
  3. 6
  4. 4

​Sequence the following sentences $(\mathrm{P}, \mathrm{Q}, \mathrm{R}, \mathrm{S})$ in a coherent passage:

$\text{P}$: Shifu's student exclaimed, "Why do you run since the bull is an illusion?"

$\text{Q}$: Shifu said, "Surely my running away from the bull is also an illusion."

$\mathrm{R}$ : Shifu once proclaimed that all life is illusion.

$\text{S}$: One day, when a bull gave him chase, Shifu began running for his life.

  1. $\text{SPRQ}$
  2. $\text{SRPQ}$
  3. $\text{RSPQ}$
  4. $\text{RPQS}$

Six bells commence tolling together and toll at interval of $2,4,6,8,10$ and $12$ seconds respectively. In $30$ minutes, how many times do they toll together?

  1. $15$
  2. $16$
  3. $20$
  4. $13$

The ratio of the number of quarters (worth $\$ 0.25$ each) to the number of dimes (worth $\$ 0.10$ each) to the number of nickels (worth $\$ 0.05$ each) in a jar is $9: 3: 2$. If the total value of the quarters and dimes is $\$ 17.85$, what is the total value of the nickels?
  1. $\$ 0.45$
  2. $\$ 0.50$
  3. $\$ 0.70$
  4. $\$ 0.35$

Consider that nodes in slotted-Aloha transmit in each slot with probability $p$. Suppose that a given channel has exactly $8$ nodes. What is the probability that there is a collision in a given slot?

  1. $1-(1-p)^8$
  2. $1-8 p(1-p)^7-(1-p)^8$
  3. $1-8 p(1-p)^7$
  4. $(1-p)^8$

Suppose you wanted to insert the following elements into a binary search tree of integers: $90,3,16,7,12,38,50$. Which of the following insertion orders will result in a complete binary tree (where all levels are fully filled except possibly for the last level, which is filled from left to right)?

  1. $16,7,3,12,50,38,90$
  2. $16,38,3,12,50,90,7$
  3. $7,16,3,90,12,50,38$
  4. $16,3,12,50,90,7,38$

Let $D(n, j)$ be the number of ways to write $n$ as a sum of integers $\left\{a_{1}, \ldots, a_{j}\right\}$, where each $a_{i}$ is an integer and used at most once.

For example, if $a_{1}=1, a_{2}=2, a_{3}=3$, and $a_{4}=4$, there are two ways to make $n=5$ from $\left\{a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, a_{4}\right\}: 5=2+3$ and $5=1+4$. Thus, $D(5,4)=2$.

Which recurrence relation correctly computes $D(n, k)$ ?

  1. $D(n, j)=D\left(n-a_{j}, j-1\right)+D(n, j-1)$
  2. $D(n, j)=D\left(n-a_{j}, j\right)+D(n, j-1)$
  3. $D(n, j)=D(n-1, j)+D(n, j-1)$
  4. $D(n, j)=D\left(n-a_{j}, j-1\right)+D\left(n-a_{j}, j-1\right)$

Consider two different enhancements to the design of a microprocessor.
The first enhancement $(\text{E1})$ speeds up $5 \%$ of the program execution time by $10 x$. The second enhancement $(\text{E2})$ speeds up $10 \%$ of the program execution time by $5 x$. Which optimization provides higher performance improvement? (Mark the correct answer).

  1. $\text{E1}$ provides more improvement than $\text{E2}$
  2. $\text{E2}$ provides more improvement than $\text{E1}$
  3. Both $\text{E1}$ and $\text{E2}$ provide similar improvements
  4. Problem statement does not have enough data to conclude which option is better

Suppose that a binary min-heap stores six elements with priorities $10, 20, 30, 40, 50,$ and $60$ in its array $\text{A}.$ What is the largest of these items that could be stored in $\text{A}[1]?$ (indexing starts from zero)

  1. $20$
  2. $30$
  3. $40$
  4. $50$

Where $n$ and head are pointers to the following struct type and intitallised as per the figure shown.

struct node{
    int data;
    struct node *next;
};

  1. $10$
  2. $20$
  3. $30$

Consider the regular language $\mathrm{L}=(11+11111)^*$. The minimum number of states in any DFA accepting this language is ______

Consider the following C code. Where x and y are unknown integers and have been initialized to values greater than 1.

int i = 1, j = 0;
while (i < y) {
    i = i + 1;
    if (i == x) break;
}


Which of the following statements about the variable $i$ must be true after the execution of this program?

  1. If $x>y$, then $i=y$
  2. If $x>y$, then $i=y-1$
  3. If $x>y$, then $i=x$
  4. If $x>y$, then $i=x-1$

Consider the following four cards. Suppose each card has a number on one side and a letter on the other side.
Minimum how many cards do we have to turn over to determine whether the following claim is true?
Claim: For each card, if the card has a vowel on one side, then it has an even number on the other side.

Consider the following state diagram of a finite state machine:


Which of the following is the correct description of this machine?

  1. Each output bit of the finite automaton is the OR of all the input bits seen so far.
  2. Each output bit of the finite automaton is the parity of all the input bits seen so far. Recall that the parity of a set of bits is 1 if the number of 1 s is odd and 0 if the number of 1 s is even.
  3. Each output bit of the finite automaton is the AND of all the input bits seen so far.
  4. Each output bit is the negation of the last input bit seen so far.

Ida Investigator sends large UDP datagram with a payload of size $4408$ bytes from office machine to her home machine. $4408$ bytes is size of application data without UDP header.


She runs a simple listening server on her home machine to observe the traffic. She notices something strange: packet arrives as three IP fragments at her home machine. Each delivered IP fragment is exactly $1500$ bytes, including IP headers.

The UDP header is $8$ bytes. Calculate the IP header size (in Bytes).

  1. $84$
  2. $20$
  3. $28$
  4. $92$

Let $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{X})$ be the number of leaves in a binary tree rooted at $\mathrm{T}$. Assume that $\mathrm{IsLeaf (T)}$ returns $1$ if $\mathrm{T}$ is a leaf. Which of the following observations leads to a recursive implementation?

  1. $\mathrm{C(T):=C(T . Left )+C( T. Right )}$
  2. $\mathrm{C(T):=C(T . Left )+C(T. Right )+1}$
  3. $\mathrm{C(T):=C(T . Left )+C(T. Right )+ IsLeaf (T)}$
  4. $\mathrm{C(T):=C(T . Left )+C(T . Right )+ IsLeaf (T)+1}$

Consider a system with a $6$ bit virtual address space, and $16$ byte pages/frames. The mapping from virtual page numbers to physical frame numbers of a process is $(0,8), (1,3), (2,11),$ and $(3,1).$ Note that all addresses are in decimal. Your answer must be in decimal.

Which of the following are is/true?

  1. the physical address to which  virtual address $20$ is mapped to is $52.$
  2. the physical address to which  virtual address $40$ is mapped to is $184.$
  3. The physical address to which  virtual address $20$ is mapped to is $53.$
  4. the physical address to which  virtual address $40$ is mapped to is $180.$
Given a set of values $\mathrm{R} = \set{1,2,3,4,5,6,7}$, What is the number of relations on this set which is both partial-order and equivalence relation?

Consider the following C code:

int i = 0;
int j = 0;
char *s = "abcde";
while (s[i] != '\0') {
        j = j + s[i] - 'a';
        i = i + 1;
}
printf("%d %d\n", i, j);

 

What will the program output be?

  1. 5 10
  2. 5 15
  3. 6 10
  4. 6 15

Suppose there are $n$ jobs $J_{1}, J_{2}, \ldots, J_{n}$ ready to run, with no other jobs in the system. Each job $J_{i}$ has a processing time $T_{i}$, and the jobs are arranged such that $T_{1} < T_{2} < .....< T_{n} $. what order should these jobs be executed in to minimize the average completion time?

  1. Jobs should be executed in the order $J_{1}, J_{2}, \ldots, J_{n}$.
     
  2. Jobs should be executed in the order $J_{n}, J_{n-1}, \ldots, J_{1}$.
     
  3. Jobs should be executed in the Round Robin order with the time quantum of $T_1$ units.
     
  4. Any order will result in the same average completion time.

Consider the productions $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{PQ}$ and $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{XY}$. Each of the five non-terminals $\text{A, P, Q, X}$, and $\text{Y}$ has two attributes: $s$ is a synthesized attribute, and $i$ is an inherited attribute. Consider the following rules.

  • Rule $1: \text{P} . i=\text{A} . i+2, \text{Q} . i=\text{P} . i+\text{A} . s$ and $\text{A} . s=\text{P} . s+\text{Q} . s$
  • Rule $2: \text{X} . i=\text{A} . i+\text{Y} . s$ and $\text{Y} . i=\text{X} . s+\text{A} . i$

Which one of the following is TRUE?

  1. Both Rule $1$ and Rule $2$ are $\text{L}$-attributed.
  2. Only Rule $1$ is $\text{L}$-attributed.
  3. Only Rule $2$ is $\text{L}$-attributed.
  4. Neither Rule $1$ nor Rule $2$ is $\text{L}$-attributed.

The graph of a cubic polynomial $f(x)$ is shown below. If $k$ is a constant such that $f(x)=k$ has three real solutions, which of the following could be a possible value of $k$ ?
 

  1. 3
  2. 0
  3. -7
  4. -3

Let $\mathrm{M}=(\Sigma, Q, s, A, \delta)$ and $\mathrm{M}^{\prime}=(\Sigma, Q, s, Q \backslash A, \delta)$ be arbitrary NFAs with identical alphabets, states, starting states, and transition functions, but with complementary accepting states.

$\mathrm{M}^{\prime}$ is identical to $\mathrm{M}$, except that accepting states in $M$ are non-accepting in $\mathrm{M}^{\prime}$ and vice versa.

Which of the following is/are viable possibilities (i.e. possible to be true for some NFA $M$ ) for $\mathrm{L}(\mathrm{M}), \mathrm{L}\left(\mathrm{M}^{\prime}\right)$ ?

  1. $\mathrm{L}(\mathrm{M})=\mathrm{L}\left(\mathrm{M}^{\prime}\right)$
  2. $\mathrm{L}\left(\mathrm{M}^{\prime}\right)$ is the complement of $\mathrm{L}(\mathrm{M})$
  3. $\mathrm{L}(\mathrm{M}), \mathrm{L}\left(\mathrm{M}^{\prime}\right)$ are neither same nor complementary.
  4. $\mathrm{L}(\mathrm{M}), \mathrm{L}\left(\mathrm{M}^{\prime}\right)$ are disjoint but not complementary.

Given a positive integer $d$, what is a set of frequencies for $2^d$ characters where the optimal prefix code has an associated tree of depth exactly $d$ ? (The depth of a tree is the length of the path from the root to the deepest leaf.)


Which of the following options is correct about set of frequencies for $2^d$ characters ?

  1. All characters have the same frequency $\frac{1}{2^{d}}$.
  2. Frequencies follow a geometric progression, with the largest frequency equal to $\frac{1}{2}$ and each subsequent frequency halved.
  3. Each frequency is a unique power of $\frac{1}{2}$, summing to 1 .
  4. One character has frequency $\frac{1}{2}$, and all other characters share the remaining frequency equally.

Consider the following weighted graph.


Let $X$ be the length of the shortest path from $s$ to $e$, and $Y$ be the number of different spanning trees of the graph.
What is the value of $X+Y$ ?

The function receives two inputs: $a$ and $n$. $a$ is a real number and $n$ is an integer such that $n \geq 1$. It should return
$$
\operatorname{SuperPower}(a, n)=a^{4 n-2}
$$
Note that in the expression above, the exponent of $a$ is $4 n-2$. Below is a recursive algorithm to compute SuperPower( $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{n}$ ) with some lines missing.

SuperPower(a, n)
    If ( A ) Return ( B)  // Base Case
    y := SuperPower( C, D ) // Recursive Call
    return ( E) // Mathematic expression using y and/or a
End


For the recursive algorithm, what expression should go in the spaces labeled $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{D}, \mathrm{E}$ ?

  1. A: $\mathrm{a=1}$,  $\mathrm{B}$: $\mathrm{a}^2$, $\mathrm{C}$: $a-1, \mathrm{D}: \mathrm{n}-1, \mathrm{E}: \mathrm{a} . \mathrm{y}^4$
  2. A: $\mathrm{n}=1, \mathrm{~B}: \mathrm{a}^ 2, \mathrm{C}: \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{D}: \mathrm{n}-1, \mathrm{E}: \mathrm{y} .
    \mathrm{a}^ 4$
  3. A: $\mathrm{n}=1, \mathrm{~B}: \mathrm{a}^ 2, \mathrm{C}: \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{D}: \mathrm{n}-4, \mathrm{E}: \mathrm{y}.\mathrm{a}^4$
  4. A: $\mathrm{n=1}$,  $\mathrm{B}: \mathrm{a}^2, \mathrm{C}: \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{D}: \mathrm{n-1}, \mathrm{E}: \mathrm{a} \cdot y^ 4$

Consider the following latch-like circuit which uses both NAND and NOR gates. On the right side, you are provided with a sequence of changes of the inputs A and B. By filling in the blanks, you will write the output values P and Q for each step of the changes. For each blank, the value you fill in could be one of the following: 0,1 , or X (indeterminate value).


What is the correct sequence of output values PQ for these changes?

  1. $10 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 01 \rightarrow 01$
  2. $10 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow \mathrm{XX}$
  3. $10 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 10$
  4. $10 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 10 \rightarrow 01$

The content of the registers are $\text{R}_{1} = \text{25H}, \text{R}_{2} = \text{30H}$ and $\text{R}_{3} = \text{40H}.$ The following machine instructions are executed.

  • $\text{PUSH } \{\text{R}_{1}\}$
  • $\text{PUSH } \{\text{R}_{2}\}$
  • $\text{PUSH } \{\text{R}_{3}\}$
  • $\text{POP } \{\text{R}_{1}\}$
  • $\text{POP } \{\text{R}_{2}\}$
  • $\text{POP } \{\text{R}_{3}\}$

After execution, the content of registers $\text{R}_{1},\:\text{R}_{2},\:\text{R}_{3}$ are

  1. $\text{R}_{1}=40\text{H},\:\text{R}_{2}=30\text{H},\:\text{R}_{3}=25\text{H}$
  2. $\text{R}_{1}=25\text{H},\:\text{R}_{2}=30\text{H},\:\text{R}_{3}=40\text{H}$
  3. $\text{R}_{1}=30\text{H},\:\text{R}_{2}=40\text{H},\:\text{R}_{3}=25\text{H}$

In the Internet Protocol (IP) suite of protocols, which of the following best describes the purpose of the Address Resolution Protocol?

  1. To translate Web addresses to host names
  2. To determine the IP address of a given host name
  3. To determine the hardware address of a given host name
  4. To determine the hardware address of a given IP address

It is impossible to represent which of the following in a relational schema?

  1. any mandatory participation constraint in a many-to-one relationship
  2. any mandatory participation constraint in a many-to-many relationship
  3. a one-to-one relationship
  4. a many-to-one relationship

Suppose you are network operator for an $\text{ISP}$, and your $\text{ISP}$ has two customer networks $\text{( IITB and IISc )}.$ For the sake of simplicity, let's assume that $\text{IITB}$ only has $3$ hosts with the following IP addresses, and IISc only has $2$ hosts:

  • $\text{IITB : } 18.0 .0 .1,18.0 .0 .254,18.255 .255 .254$
  • $\text{IISc :} 128.112 .0 .1$, and $128.112 .255 .254$

You have heard that memory in router line cards is expensive, so you would like to use as few entries as possible in your line cards. Your colleague at work says he has a solution that only requires two forwarding-table entries.

Give the IP prefix notation that your colleague uses to represent these two networks.

  1. $18.0 .0 .0 / 8$ and $128.112 .0 .0 / 16$
  2. $18.0.0.0/24$ and $128.112.0.0/8$
  3. $18.0.0.0/16$ and $128.112.0.0/16$
  4. $18.0.0.0/24$ and $128.112.0.0/24$

\[
F(A, B, C, D)=\sum m(0,2,5,7,8,10,12,13,14,15) \text {, }
\]
the essential prime implicants are $\_\_\_\_\_\_$.

  1. $B D, \bar{B} \bar{D}$
  2. $B D, A B$
  3. $A B, \bar{B} \bar{D}$
  4. $B D, \bar{B} \bar{D}, A B$

For automata $\text{M},$ let $\langle \text{M}\rangle$ denote some unary encoding of $\text{M},$ and $\text{L(M)}$ denote the set of strings, over $\{0,1\},$ accepted by $\text{M}.$
Which of the following languages are Turing-decidable?

  1. $\{\langle \text{M}\rangle \mid \text{M}$ is a deterministic Turing machine and $\text{M}$ accepts $010\}.$
  2. $\{\langle \text{M}\rangle \mid \text{M}$ is a nondeterministic Turing machine and $\text{M}$ accepts $010\}.$
  3. $\{\langle \text{M}\rangle \mid \text{M}$ is a DFA and $\text{M}$ does not accept $010\}.$
  4. $\left\{\langle \text{M}\rangle \mid \text{M}\right.$ is a Turing machine and $\left.\text{L(M)}=\Sigma^\ast\right\}$.

Consider the following simple context-free grammars:
$$\begin{array}{lll}\text {Grammar } \text{G}_1 & \text {Grammar } \text{G}_2 & \text {Grammar } \text{G}_3 \\ \text{S} \rightarrow \text{A} & \text{S} \rightarrow \text{A} & \text{S} \rightarrow \text{A} \\ \text{A} \rightarrow \varepsilon & \text{A} \rightarrow \varepsilon & \text{A} \rightarrow \varepsilon \\ \text{A} \rightarrow b b \text{A} & \text{A} \rightarrow b \text{A} b & \text{A} \rightarrow \text{A} b b\end{array}$$

The start symbols are $\text{S}$, the non-terminals are $\text{S}$ and $\text{A}$, and $b$ is a terminal symbol. You may also treat $\$$ as a terminal to represent end-of-file. Note that these grammars all generate the same language $=\text{L}\left(\text{G}_1\right)=\text{L}\left(\text{G}_2\right)=\text{L}\left(\text{G}_3\right)$ : strings consisting of even numbers of $b$ symbols (including $0$ of them).

Which of the following is/are TRUE?

  1. $\text{G}_1$ is $\text{LL(1)}$
  2. $\text{G}_2$ is $\text{LL(1)}$
  3. $\text{G}_3$ is $\text{LL(1)}$
  4. Language generated by these grammar is $\text{LL(1)}$

Here is a definition for a set of trees called GO trees.
Basis: A single vertex with no edges is a GO tree. The root is the only vertex in the tree.

Recursive rule: If $\mathrm{T1}$ and $\mathrm{T2}$ are GO trees, then a new GO tree $\mathrm{T}$' can be constructed by first placing $\mathrm{T1}$ to the left of $\mathrm{T2}$ , adding a new vertex v at the top and then adding an edge between $\mathrm{v}$ and the root of $\mathrm{T1}$ and an edge between $\mathrm{v}$ and the root of $\mathrm{T2}$ . The new vertex v is the root of $\mathrm{T'}$.


Exclusion statement: $\mathrm{T}$ is a GO tree only if $\mathrm{T}$ is the tree described in the Basis or $\mathrm{T}$ can be constructed by repeatedly applying the recursive rule starting with the tree given in the basis.
Which of the following trees is/are NOT a GO tree?
In a number system of base $r$, the equation $x^{2}-12 x+37=0$ has $x=8$ as one of its solutions. The value of $r$ is $\_\_\_\_\_\_\_$.

Given the following grammar with nonterminals $\mathrm{S}, \mathrm{A}$, and B .
$\mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{AaBb}$
$\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ab} \mid \mathrm{b}$
$\mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{aB} \mid \mathrm{a}$
Which of the following sentences is/are valid ones in the language generated by this grammar?

  1. baab
  2. bbbab
  3. bbaaaa
  4. bbaab

A lexical analyzer uses the following patterns to recognize three tokens T1, T2, and T3 over the alphabet $\{\mathrm{x, y}\}$ :

  • T1: $\mathrm{x}$
  • T2: $\mathrm{xxxx}$
  • T3: $\mathrm{x}^{4n}\mathrm{y}$ for $n \geq 1$

The analyzer outputs the token that matches the longest possible prefix.
For which of the following strings will the lexical analyzer backtrack while tokenizing the string?

  1. $\mathrm{x}$
  2. $\mathrm{x x x x x x x x y}$ ( 8 $\mathrm{x}$ characters)
  3. $\mathrm{x x x x x x x x x x x x x x y}$ ( 13 $\mathrm{x}$ characters)
  4. $\mathrm{x x}$

In the following network, node $\mathrm{S}$ transmits packets that pass through a tandem network of $16$ routers, and arrive at the destination $\mathrm{D}$. The bit rate of all links is $\mathrm{R}=1 \;\mathrm{Mbit} / \mathrm{sec}$. The maximum packet size in the network is $500$ Bytes. Ignore the header size. The one-way propagation delay on each link is $10\; \mathrm{msec}$. Assume that there is no error in transmission in the network, and the size of ACK packets is negligible.


How long does it take to transmit a file of size $50,000$ Bytes if S and D use Stop-and-Wait ARQ?

  1. $23.8$ seconds
  2. $40.8$ Seconds
  3. $36.7$ seconds
  4. $7.53$ seconds

Find the inverse of the matrix $\left(\begin{array}{ll}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{array}\right)$.

  1. $\left(\begin{array}{cc}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -4\end{array}\right)$
     
  2. $\left(\begin{array}{cc}4 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{array}\right)$
     
  3. $\left(\begin{array}{cc}\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{3}{2} \\ -1 & 2\end{array}\right)$
     
  4. $\left(\begin{array}{cc}-2 & 1 \\ \frac{3}{2} & -\frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right)$

In a computer with a cache memory interposed between the processor and the primary memory, the cache is $k$-way set-associative (for some fixed $k$ ); i.e., each location in primary memory "maps to" (can be cached in) any of $k$ locations in the cache. Let there be $\text{P}$ locations in primary memory and $\text{C}$ locations in the cache.
On the average, how many different locations in the primary memory map to a particular location in the cache if $k=2$?

  1. $1$
  2. $2$
  3. $\text{P / C}$
  4. $\text{2 P / C}$

The number of sets in two independent caches C1 and C2 is same. C1 is a 2-way associative cache with 32 byte blocks where as C2 is an 8 -way associative cache with 256 byte blocks. The total storage space of C2 is _____ times larger than C1 .

Consider the following schedule:

T1    R(A) W(C) R(B)
T2 R(A)R(B)      
T3R(A)    W(B)   
T4   W(A)   R(C) 


What is the set of edges of the conflict dependency graph for the schedule? We write $\left(T_{i}, T_{j}\right)$ if there exists a directed edge from $T_{i}$ to $T_{j}$.
